CVE-2025-35939.title: Craft CMS stores user-provided content in session files
CVE-2025-35939.description: Craft CMS stores arbitrary content provided by unauthenticated users in session files. This content could be accessed and executed, possibly using an independent vulnerability. Craft CMS redirects requests that require authentication to the login page and generates a session file on the server at '/var/lib/php/sessions'. Such session files are named 'sess_[session_value]', where '[session_value]' is provided to the client in a 'Set-Cookie' response header. Craft CMS stores the return URL requested by the client without sanitizing parameters. Consequently, an unauthenticated client can introduce arbitrary values, such as PHP code, to a known local file location on the server. Craft CMS versions 5.7.5 and 4.15.3 have been released to address this issue.

kev.name: Craft CMS External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter Vulnerability
kev.required_action: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions, follow applicable BOD 22-01 guidance for cloud services, or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.

CVE-2026-135256.title: MISP Warninglist ReDoS via Unbounded Regex Backtracking
CVE-2026-135256.description:
MISP contains a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in its Warninglist feature. Warninglist entries of type "regex" are evaluated against attribute values without any backtracking limit. An authenticated user with permission to add or import warninglist entries can supply a crafted regular expression pattern that triggers excessive backtracking in the PCRE engine, causing sustained CPU consumption and denial of service.

Additionally, imported warninglists were not validated for syntactic correctness before replacing existing entries, allowing malformed or malicious patterns to be persisted and later evaluated without prior rejection.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated account with the ability to create, edit, or import warninglist entries (users below site-admin level can add entries).
- The target MISP instance has at least one warninglist of type "regex" that will be evaluated against incoming attribute values.

applicability check is nested inside a test for the presence of a `Domain` attribute, so a cookie

`MetadataTransfer`, which carries the stored cookie to outlinks, ever considers the host that issued

CVE-2026-99651.title: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes
CVE-2026-99651.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes

Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabling
merge_across_nodes resets this count to 1, even if per-node roots were
previously allocated.

So when toggling "merge_across_nodes" 0 -> 1 -> 0, a scan that starts
while the setting is 1 and continues after switching back to 0 can
encounter stale unstable tree roots, resulting in UAF.

Only root is allowed to change "merge_across_nodes", and the documented
sequence is: "merge_across_nodes setting can be changed only when there
are no ksm shared pages in the system: set run 2 to unmerge pages first,
then to 1 after changing merge_across_nodes, to remerge according to the
new setting."

Let's fix it by tracking in ksm_nr_node_ids the actual number of
allocated tree roots.

remove_all_stable_nodes() and ksm_check_stable_tree() will now scan
more tree roots (skipping the empty ones), which is harmless.
